tollmaster.name: the Tollmaster
tollmaster.desc: Holds the Shannon bridges and charges a toll on every road.

glen_lords.name: the glen lords
glen_lords.desc: Hold the hills and the glens with spears and dogs.

church.name: the holy places
church.desc: Hermits, wells and ruined oratories that still keep the Office.

fishers.name: the coast folk
fishers.desc: Fishers and boatmen who trade salt fish along the strands.

bog.name: the bog folk
bog.desc: Turf-cutters who live where the old turbines stand.

nodes.name: Inishkeel
nodes.desc: A drowned church on a tidal island. Its bells are said to ring at low water.

nodes.name: Three Wells
nodes.desc: Three holy wells beside a roofless oratory.

nodes.name: Lough Dearg
nodes.desc: A hermit's island in a grey lake, reached by a boat that may not be there.
nodes.label: left

nodes.name: Knockmore
nodes.desc: A stone hold on a hill, with dogs at the gate and a lord who keeps accounts.
nodes.label: left

nodes.name: Slieve Bloom
nodes.desc: A high hold where the glen lords meet in autumn to divide the cattle.

nodes.name: Ballyhale
nodes.desc: A market town at the Shannon crossing, where the Tollmaster's men count every cart.
nodes.label: left

nodes.name: Kilcullen
nodes.desc: A busy town with a bridge, a fair and a reeve who writes everything down.

nodes.name: the Bog of Allen
nodes.desc: Old turbines stand dead on the bog. Some still turn in a strong wind.
nodes.label: above

nodes.name: the Glen of Imaal
nodes.desc: Scattered farms in a green glen, with a hurling field and a wary headman.
nodes.label: left

nodes.name: Kilmore Quay
nodes.desc: A harbour of fishing boats and smoked fish, where the sea wind never stops.
nodes.label: left

nodes.name: the Clare cliffs
nodes.desc: A ruined signal tower on the cliffs, where the coast folk leave their dead boats.
